question: Can Garcia's 2010 Candaba wetland fish paper be reviewed at species level from an accessible full text?

source.citation: Garcia, L. M. B. (2010). Species composition and length-weight relationship of fishes in the Candaba wetland on Luzon Island, Philippines. Journal of Applied Ichthyology, 26(6), 946–948. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1439-0426.2010.01516.x
source.accessNote: The publisher-indexed abstract was available in search results. Direct page retrieval returned HTTP 403; the direct PDF endpoint returned HTTP 403 and the pdfdirect endpoint timed out. Exact-title and DOI searches did not identify a clearly author- or institution-hosted full text in the results reviewed. This bounded search does not prove that no copy exists.

publisherAbstractFindings.dominantFamilyDescription: Cyprinids comprised the greatest number of species.

scopeAndAccessLimits.studyScope: Historical fish catches attributed to Candaba wetland in central Luzon; the accessible abstract gives a two-year period and aggregate richness only.
scopeAndAccessLimits.siteResolutionLimit: The abstract does not provide named sampling stations, a wetland-to-station matrix, coordinates, vouchers, or individual taxon dates.
scopeAndAccessLimits.fullTextLimit: The species table and full methods were not reviewed because the publisher full-text routes were inaccessible in this pass.
scopeAndAccessLimits.rightsLimit: No article-specific open license or reuse permission was verified. Do not reproduce or derive public app rows from an inaccessible article table.

alternativeSearch.approach: Searched the exact article title and DOI for a lawful author/institution-hosted copy and checked the publisher abstract/PDF endpoints.
alternativeSearch.result: No clearly identified author- or institution-hosted copy was found in the bounded search results. This is an access gap, not proof that a copy does not exist.
alternativeSearch.outreach: No email or request was sent.

nextAction: If species-level extraction becomes necessary, use an authorized library or author-provided copy, record its provenance and license separately, then review the full table and station/date/voucher context before any taxon crosswalk.

sources.supports: Official title, DOI, citation, publication date, publisher abstract counts, and broad catch period.
Attempted official full-text route; direct retrieval returned HTTP 403 during this review.
